key_insight: The paper shows that memory should not be gated with a one-size-fits-all policy: facts are more useful when gating is personalized to each user’s future retrieval behavior. It turns delayed, one-sided feedback into training labels for deciding which memories to keep.
problem_solved: Long-term memory systems in language-model agents have limited storage, so they must decide which extracted facts to retain. Existing gating methods are usually shared across users and miss individual patterns of what gets reused later.
method: Proposes a retrieval-based labeling strategy that marks each fact by whether it is later retrieved and used in responses.
Learns a personalized memory-gating policy at the fact level, rather than using a universal gate for all users.
Uses delayed one-sided feedback from future interactions to supervise memory selection.
impact: This helps AI agents store more useful memories for each user, improving personalization while keeping memory banks efficient. For practitioners, it offers a practical way to reduce wasted memory storage and improve long-term conversational quality.

paper_title: Learning Personalized Memory Gating from Delayed One-Sided Feedback
paper_authors: Kaixuan Ji, Zixiang Chen, Wenting Zhao, Cheng Qian, Heng Wang
